''What it changes, and why:'' 

''Sources:'' 

''PDF (optional, for a long proposal):'' [[Special:Upload|upload it]], then replace this line with its name, as in <nowiki>[[Media:Name of the file.pdf]]</nowiki>.

'''Proposed text''' (TeX). Paste the blocks that change, copied from the TeX source of the page and edited (a section with its title, or a statement or a proof with its label), or the whole TeX source of the page: only what changes is applied, and there is no limit of length. A new block goes after an existing one: put the line <code>%% after: title or label</code> just before it.
<pre>
\section{Title of the section}
The new text of the section.
</pre>

'''New references''' (papers that are not yet on [[Literature]], one per line: \bibitem{AuthorYear} A. Author and B. Author, Title of the paper, Journal 12 (2020), 345–678, doi:... or arXiv:...; cite them in the text with the same key):
<pre>
</pre>

~~<includeonly>~~</includeonly><noinclude>
The form of a new proposal, opened by the link ''new proposal'' under the title of a page in the wiki (''Propose a change'' in the edition opens a box of its own, see [[Template:Proposal/Preload-popup]]). Once the proposal is accepted, an editor applies it with <code>wikitex.py apply-proposal</code>, which reads the blocks in the box ''Proposed text'' and lists the lines of the box ''New references'' (they go into the reference catalogue first). The split signature at the end becomes four tildes in the new topic. See [[How to contribute#Proposing a change|How to contribute]].</noinclude>
